entries.title: Propaganda in moving image and sound, 1924–1945: Bolzano and Alto Adige in Luce films and photographs, foreign and German-language eyes, feature films and their censorship, the EIAR station, and the cinemas of the city
text: The working notes on propaganda in moving image and sound: the Luce films that can be watched and what they show, the Luce photographs, feature films and their censorship, the radio station, and the cinemas of the city and the valleys.

Two of Luis Trenker's films were approved for Italy and banned in the provinces of Bolzano and Trento alone. In November 1935 Bolzano's Edenkino began to call itself “Cinema Luce”. Nothing found, film or photograph, shows the Option of 1939.
facts: Six threads: watchable Luce films with stills and full records (§1), the Luce photo archive (§2), other eyes (§3), feature films and censorship (§4), radio and sound (§5), cinema as an instrument in the city (§6) (notes 15)

Italian film censorship banned Trenker's 'Il figliuol prodigo' (1935) and 'L'imperatore della California' (1937) from public screens in the provinces of Bolzano and Trento while approving them for the rest of Italy (notes 15, §4, [V])
From 27 November 1935, nine days after the League sanctions were to enter into force, the Edenkino of Bolzano advertised itself as 'Cinema Luce (ex Edenkino)' (notes 15, §6, [V])
Luce photographed the Brenner meeting of 4 October 1940, for which no Luce film story had been found (notes 15, §2, [V])
No Luce film or photograph found shows the 1939 Option; of the photos found by place name, more were taken in Rome and Ostia (54) than in Bolzano (21) (notes 15, §1–2, [V])
British Pathé, Learning on Screen, the Bundesarchiv film portal and Wikimedia Commons could not be read by script on 12 November 2026; foreign newsreels remain leads (notes 15, §3)

entries.title: Italia Taglia: censorship records of the Trenker films (1930–1940) and of films titled for Bolzano, the Brenner, the Dolomites and the Tyrol (1921–1942), 13 records
text: Thirteen records from the Italian film-censorship database: seven films under Luis Trenker's name, 1930 to 1940, and six whose titles name Bolzano, the Brenner, the Dolomites or the Tyrol. Two Trenker films passed for the rest of Italy with one condition. “Figliuol prodigo”, September 1935: “Le proiezioni in pubblico del film … sono vietate nelle Provincie di Bolzano e Trento.” “L'imperatore della California”, January 1937, the same.
The reasons are not in the records. The database lists the second as “Imperatrice (L') di California”, a slip for “Der Kaiser von Kalifornien”.
facts: Seven Trenker films are listed under his name: 'Cavalieri della montagna' (visto 26066, 31 Oct 1930), 'Figliuol prodigo' (28980, 1935), 'Imperatrice (L') di California' [so listed; the film is 'L'imperatore della California'] (29418, 1936–37), 'Condottieri' (29671, 1937), 'La grande conquista' (30355, 1938), 'Lettere d'amore dall'Engadina' (30641, 1939), 'Il ribelle della montagna' (31160, 1940) (file; notes 15, §4, [V])

'Figliuol prodigo' (Der verlorene Sohn), 'Approvata con riserva', 31 Aug 1935: 'Le proiezioni in pubblico del film … sono vietate nelle Provincie di Bolzano e Trento. (settembre 1935)' (file, record FACNW0002815, [V])

'L'imperatore della California' (Der Kaiser von Kalifornien; listed by the database as 'Imperatrice (L') di California'), visto 29418: 'La proiezione di questa pellicola è vietata nelle Provincie di Trento e Bolzano. (gennaio 1937)' (file, record FWOIRV000278, [V])
'Condottieri' was recognised as a national film and admitted to the compulsory-screening benefit of R.D.L. 5 ottobre 1933 n. 1414 and Legge 13 giugno 1935 n. 1083 (file, record FWOVON000524, [V])

'S.M. il Re a Bolzano', production Zuliani, 250 m, visto 22963, dates 15 and 19 Aug 1926: a non-Luce film of the king in Bolzano, a month after the monument's first stone was laid on 12 July 1926 in his presence (file, [V]; it.wikipedia, 'Monumento alla Vittoria (Bolzano)', [W]); that it shows the ceremony is an inference, [INF]

Also: 'Bellezze italiche: da Bolzano a Cortina' (U.C.I., 1921), 'Quarta adunata sciatoria Valligiani al Brennero' (1922), the Austrian 'Dramma fra le Dolomiti' (1921, cut for its nihilist conspiracy), 'Dolomiti italiane' (1923) and 'Fra i monti del Tirolo' (Reichsbahnzentrale für den Deutschen Reiseverkehr, 1942) (file, [V])

'Montagne in fiamme' (Berge in Flammen) and 'Der Rebell' were not found in the database by title or director; the column 'dates_as_listed' keeps the dates in page order because the page does not label each one (file; notes 15, §4, Gaps)

Title corrected on 12 November 2026 after the author's check: the database's own fields read 'Imperatrice (L') di California' and 'titolo corretto: Imperatrice di California (L')' beside 'titolo originale: Der Kaiser von Kalifornien' (record FWOIRV000278, [V]); the Italian release title is 'L'imperatore della California' (film listings found by search, [SS])

entries.title: Atti Parlamentari, Camera dei Deputati, tornata del 6 febbraio 1926, pages 5401–5404: Mussolini on Germany and the Alto Adige
text: The stenographic record of the Chamber of Deputies on 6 February 1926, when Mussolini answered Bavaria's prime minister over South Tyrol. “Veramente del confine del Brennero si può dire che è un confine segnato dalla mano infallibile di Dio. (Vivissimi applausi)”. The Germans of Alto Adige, he says, are not a national minority but “una reliquia etnica”.
He announces that in Bolzano, on the foundations laid for a German victory monument, a monument to Cesare Battisti will rise. The record notes: “Si canta l'inno Giovinezza”. No recording was found.
facts: Stenographic record of the Chamber sitting of 6 Feb 1926: Farinacci's urgent question on relations with Germany after a speech by the Bavarian prime minister Held, and Mussolini's answer (file, pp. 5401–5404, [V])
'Veramente del confine del Brennero si può dire che è un confine segnato dalla mano infallibile di Dio. (Vivissimi applausi)' (file, p. 5403, [V])

'Renderemo italiana quella regione, perchè è italiana … italiana geograficamente, italiana storicamente'; 'I tedeschi nell'Alto Adige non rappresentano una minoranza nazionale, rappresentano una reliquia etnica' (file, p. 5403, [V]; the OCR reads 'Penderemo')
'L'Italia fascista può, se sarà necessario, portare oltre il suo tricolore, abbassarlo mai!', after which the record notes 'Si canta l'inno Giovinezza' (file, pp. 5403–5404, [V])

Mussolini announces that in Bolzano, 'sulle stesse fondamenta sulle quali doveva sorgere il monumento della vittoria tedesca, erigeremo un monumento a Cesare Battisti'; Farinacci invites the deputies to open a subscription 'per un monumento a Cesare Battisti a Bolzano' (file, pp. 5401, 5404, [V])
No recording of this speech was found; the Discoteca di Stato's Mussolini series is reported to begin in October 1935 (notes 15, §5, [SS])
Seen in the image: a printed page headed 'Atti Parlamentari — 5403 — Camera dei Deputati', 'Tornata del 6 febbraio 1926', in two columns, with stage directions in italics

entries.title: Istituto Luce, Foto Attualità: 144 photograph records found under "bolzano", "brennero" and "alto adige", 1928–1943
text: An index of 144 photographs in the Istituto Luce's news-photo fund found under “bolzano”, “brennero” and “alto adige”, 1928 to 1943, in 28 stories. The first research pass had counted the hits and not opened them. More were taken in Rome and Ostia (54), where the province's delegations were shown to the capital, than in Bolzano (21); the Brenner has 28.
Seventeen of the “bolzano” hits show the cruiser of that name. None shows the Option, and none the Semirurali.
facts: The earlier pass counted 73 'Foto Attualità (1927–1956)' hits for 'bolzano' and did not open them (notes 02, §1, Gaps); this index holds those 73 plus 43 for 'brennero' and 30 for 'alto adige', 144 records after removing doubles, in 28 photo stories (file; notes 15, §2, [V])
Measured: by place of the shot, Roma 40, Ostia 14, Bolzano 21, the Brenner 28 (three spellings), the rest blank or regional; 17 of the 'bolzano' hits show the cruiser Bolzano, not the city (file)

Stories in Bolzano: the monument's inauguration (13.07.1928, 11 photos), a youth gymnastic display in the stadium (08.06.1931), the 'riconoscenza' rally (04.09.1938), a fur auction in the Palazzo Mercantile (16.01.1942), 'Ragazzi russi in grigio-verde' (10.06.1943) (file, [V])
Stories at the Brenner: Hitler's arrival (03.05.1938, 15 photos by Spartaco Appetiti), the meetings of 18.03.1940 (8) and 04.10.1940 (7) (file, [V])

Province shown in Rome: South Tyrolean union delegates at Palazzo Chigi (24.04.1928), bands of the Brenner and Bressanone (07.01.1929), Alto Adige young fascists (19.08.1931, 12), Giovani Italiane of the province at Ostia and Palazzo Venezia (29.03.1932, 17), 250 Bolzano giovani fasciste before Mussolini (10.12.1938) (file, [V])
No photograph of the 1939 Option and none of the Semirurali was found under these three words (file; notes 15, §2, [V])

entries.title: A Bolzano inaugurazione del monumento alla Vittoria d'Italia (Giornale Luce A0137)
text: The Luce newsreel of the inauguration of the Monument to Victory, July 1928: four minutes and forty-three seconds, silent. Priests bless the monument, the king sits on the royal stand, a South Tyrolean band plays, the procession crosses the Talvera bridge, Giovani Italiane and Balilla march past.
The catalogue notes that Giuriati gives the official speech “ma è nascosto dalla feluca del valletto”: hidden by a footman's hat. The reel's other story is “Ardite esibizioni di cowboy”.
facts: Giornale Luce A / A0137, code IL5000048984, clip A013701, catalogue date 07/1928, 4'43", black and white, silent; direzione artistica Mario Craveri (record, [V])

Sequences include 'un gruppo di tre sacerdoti benedice il monumento', 'sul palco reale, Vittorio Emanuele III – Giuriati pronuncia il discorso ufficiale, ma è nascosto dalla feluca del valletto', 'la banda musicale altoatesina', 'il corteo traversa il ponte sulla Talvera', 'sfilata di giovani italiane e di balilla' (record, [V])

Silent: the speech that the new EIAR station relayed to loudspeakers in Piazza Walther the same day is, in the film, a man hidden by a footman's hat (record; notes 02, §3, [V]; the pairing is an inference, [INF])
The same reel's other story is 'Ardite esibizioni di cowboy' (record, [V])
Plays on the Luce catalogue page through the Archivio Luce Cinecittà YouTube video bMqh-q3eUJI (record; manifest)

entries.title: Istituto Luce, "S.M. il Re inaugura il monumento ai caduti di Bolzano", three photographs
text: Three of eleven Luce photographs of the inauguration, filed on 13 July 1928. Soldiers line the square before the monument with arms raised; men carry flags past the royal stand; a group poses between the columns.
Luce's title and captions do not call it the Monument to Victory. It is “il monumento ai caduti”, a memorial to the fallen, with “enormi colonne che raffigurano dei fasci littori”.
facts: Luce photo story of 11 photographs, catalogue date 13.07.1928, author 'Istituto Nazionale Luce'; codes A00004247 ('Inquadratura del monumento ai caduti e della piazza antistante dove sono schierati i soldati'), A00004249, A00004252 (records, [V])
Luce's caption calls the Monument to Victory a 'monumento ai caduti', a war memorial (records, [V]; notes 15, §2)
The catalogue date is the day after the inauguration of 12 July 1928 given in the earlier notes; the date on the record may be the date of filing (notes 02, §1, [V]; inference, [INF])

A00004249: 'Un gruppo di autorità locali (?), tra cui una giovane signora che indossa un elegante abito alla moda, posa in cima al monumento ai caduti, tra le enormi colonne che raffigurano dei fasci littori' (record, [V])

Seen in the image (A00004247): the monument's front with its columns, an eagle relief and a lettered band above, steps, soldiers in helmets lined up in the foreground with raised arms, flags on poles, street lamps; watermark 'ISTITUTO LUCE'
Seen in the image (A00004249): eleven men in dark suits and a young woman in a light dress and cloche hat standing on a wet stone floor between two large columns
Seen in the image (A00004252): men carrying flags march across an open square before a stand hung with drapery and a crown, trees behind

entries.title: Radiorario, 9–16 September 1928, no. 37: "Ricezioni della Stazione di Bolzano"
text: The radio weekly prints listeners' letters about the new Bolzano station. From Cagliari, 30 August 1928: “ho captato l'onda di Bolzano”. From Forlì: the tourist board's bulletin came “forte e chiaro in altoparlante”, though disturbed by Bern. Near Pisa, “ora udiamo Bolzano … tutte le sere”.
A station of 200 watts, opened for the monument's inauguration, was heard at night in Sardinia. A year later the same weekly called it the Italian station most damaged by interference.
facts: Radiorario Anno IV no. 37, 9–16 Sept 1928, 'organo ufficiale dell'E.I.A.R.'; on printed page 4 (PDF page 6) a column 'Ricezioni della Stazione di Bolzano' prints listeners' letters (file, [V])

Cagliari, 30 Aug 1928: 'ho captato l'onda di Bolzano percependo sufficientemente bene una dizione «sulla stretta della mano» un ballabile, le notizie Stefani, e la fine della trasmissione' (file, [V])

Forlì, 2 Sept 1928: 'ho ascoltato il giornale dell'Enit dalla Stazione di Bolzano. Forte e chiaro in altoparlante ma disturbato da un sibilo continuo dovuto ad interferenza della stazione di Berna' (file, [V])
Other letters from Portogruaro, Borgosesia, Rovereto ('90 km') and Pisa (Calci), where 'ora udiamo Bolzano (musica, comunicazioni e notizie) tutte le sere' (file, [V])

A 200-watt station opened for the monument's inauguration was heard, at night, in Sardinia and Tuscany: a station built for the place also carried the place's name to the nation (notes 02, §3, [V]; notes 15, §5, [INF])
In 1929 the same weekly called Bolzano the Italian station most damaged by interference, 'trasmettendo sopra un'onda comune' (Radiocorriere 1929 no. 29, not held; notes 15, §5, [V])

Seen in the image: a magazine page headed 'RADIORARIO' and '4', with a photograph of a sculpted trophy for the Monza Grand Prix at top and three columns below, the middle one headed 'Ricezioni della Stazione di Bolzano'

entries.title: Istituto Luce, "Bolzano – Saggio ginnico di Giovani fascisti", two photographs
text: Two Luce photographs filed on 8 June 1931: Balilla drawn up in rows on a marked field, and Piccole Italiane kneeling with one arm stretched up, men in suits and uniforms behind them. The captions place both “nello stadio di Bolzano”.
Which ground that was in 1931 is not stated.
facts: Luce photo story of two photographs, catalogue date 08.06.1931, place 'Bolzano', themes 'balilla; esercitazioni ginniche' and 'piccole italiane; esercitazioni ginniche'; photographer not named (records A00030295, A00030296, [V])
Captions: 'Balilla schierati nello stadio di Bolzano per un saggio ginnico'; 'Piccole italiane durante un saggio ginnico allo stadio di Bolzano' (records, [V])
Which ground 'lo stadio di Bolzano' was in 1931 is not stated; the place is left open (notes 15, §2, Gaps)
Seen in the image (A00030295): several hundred children in white tops and dark shorts or skirts in rows on a large field marked with lines, a long wall and a road behind; watermark 'ARCHIVIO LUCE'

entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 14 June 1934, page 5
text: The Alpenzeitung prints the route of Luce's travelling cinema through the province: sixty places from Vandoies on 10 June to Laives and Vadena, Bolzano on the 24th. It shows farming films on the agriculture ministry's instruction, and with them newsreels of “die letzten Weltereignisse”, clearer for the farmer, the paper says, “als manch langer Zeitungsartikel”.
On the same page: the setting up of private schools for teaching German.
facts: 'Landwirtschaftliche Filme': 'Bereits Ende Mai hat die Kinounternehmung „Luce“ eine Rundfahrt durch unsere Provinz unternommen, auf welcher sie auf Anregung und nach Weisung des Ackerbauministeriums in allen größeren Ortschaften Lehrfilme landwirtschaftlichen Inhaltes vorführt' (image, [V])

Besides teaching films, 'führt die „Luce“ aber noch eine ganze Reihe von Streifen vor, auf denen die letzten Weltereignisse dargestellt sind', clearer for the farmer 'als manch langer Zeitungsartikel'; each show is explained by an expert of the Cattedra Ambulante (image, [V])

The full itinerary of the 'Wanderkino': 60 places from Vandoies (10 June) through the Isarco and Adige valleys, Val Gardena, Bolzano (24 June) and Gries (25 June), Val Venosta, to Laives and Vadena (image, [V])
Same page: 'Deutscher Sprachunterricht – Die Errichtung von Privatschulen für den Unterricht der deutschen Sprache', and 'Kino-Nachrichten' for the Edenkino and Centralkino (image, [V])

The earliest travelling cinema found is that of the Opera Nazionale Combattenti, 'für die landwirtschaftliche Propaganda', from 15 June 1927, with 'landwirtschaftliche und patriotische Films' for small villages (Alpenzeitung, 15 June 1927, Europeana page 3 of 6, not held; notes 15, §6, [V])

Seen in the image: a full newspaper page in Fraktur headed 'Aus Bolzano Stadt und Land', dated 'Donnerstag, den 14. Juni 1934', with a long column 'Deutscher Sprachunterricht' at left, a column 'Landwirtschaftliche Filme' in the middle and an advertisement for the telephone at lower right
Europeana gives this page as canvas 3 of 4 of the issue; the printed page number is 5 (file; manifest)

entries.title: Italia. Bolzano (Istituto Luce documentary D046109)
text: A Luce documentary of 1935, fourteen and a half minutes with sound: Mussolini in Bolzano and at the army manoeuvres with the king. He stands in the car giving the salute, “un gigantesco ritratto di Mussolini è appeso ad un palazzo”, and inside the monument he honours the busts of Battisti, Filzi and Chiesa.
The manoeuvres themselves are filmed from Revò in the Val di Non, in the province of Trento. The catalogue transcribes no commentary.
facts: Code IL3000090303, film code D046109, 1935, 14'37", black and white, sound, Italian; production Istituto Nazionale Luce: 'Il documentario mostra la visita di Mussolini a Bolzano e la sua partecipazione insieme a Vittorio Emanuele III alla grandi manovre nel bolzanino' (record, [V])

In Bolzano: 'il Duce in piedi sull'auto risponde a tutti facendo il saluto romano', 'un gigantesco ritratto di Mussolini è appeso ad un palazzo', homage inside the monument to 'i busti marmorei dedicati a Battisti, Filzi e Chiesa', the Istituto Duchessa di Pistoia, the ONB (record, [V])

The manoeuvres: 'carrellata panoramica dall'osservatorio di Revò', 'il Re e Mussolini presenziano alla grande esercitazione', Badoglio and Starace, 'il Duce vicino ad un apparecchio radio da campo', and at the end 'carrellata panoramica sulla zona della Val di Non … Mussolini finisce il suo discorso' (record, [V])
So Mussolini was at the 1935 manoeuvres, but the record places them in the Val di Non (Revò), in the province of Trento, although the newsreel title says 'nel Bolzanino' (record; notes 02, §1, [V])
The record transcribes no spoken commentary; what the speaker says has to be heard on the portal (notes 15, §1, Gaps)
Seen in the image: a dense crowd round a car strewn with flowers, men in dark uniforms among them; burned-in timecode 'TCR 01:22:35:11'

entries.title: Mussolini visita il confine italo-austriaco presso il Passo del Brennero (Giornale Luce B0742)
text: Mussolini at the border stone on the Brenner, 4 September 1935, one minute forty-one. A girl gives him flowers, troops are drawn up, and “il Duce arriva sul cippo del confine”.
The stone is a ritual object in Luce films of 1928, 1935 and 1938. Two stories later the same reel shows the opening of a new road from Salzburg to the Grossglockner.
facts: Giornale Luce B / B0742, code IL5000020066, clip B074202, 04/09/1935, 1'41", sound; direzione artistica Arturo Gemmiti (record, [V])

Sequences: 'calorose manifestazioni di entusiasmo della gente', 'il Duce riceve un mazzo di fiori da una bambina', 'reparti militari schierati accolgono il Duce', 'il Duce arriva sul cippo del confine' (record, [V])
The same reel carried 'inaugurazione di una nuova autostrada da Salisburgo al massiccio del Gross Glockner', two stories after the Brenner (record, [V])
The boundary stone appears as a ritual object in Luce films of 1928, 1935 and 1938 (notes 02, §4, [V]; this row, record)

entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 27 November 1935, page 5
text: From this day the Alpenzeitung lists the Edenkino as “Cinema Luce (ex Edenkino)”. The League of Nations sanctions against Italy had been due to take effect nine days earlier, and a later comment ties the renaming to Anthony Eden; the paper gives no reason.
On the same page pupils of the commercial school are taken to the Ethiopian-war film “Von Adua nach Aksum”, and a drawing shows the new centre planned at the Monument to Victory.
facts: 'Kino-Programme': 'Cinema Luce (ex Edenkino). Heute Italiens berühmte Komiker: Leda Gloria, die Brüder De Filippo …', and the Central-Kino with Franziska Gaal in 'Gruß und Kuß, Veronika' (image, [V])

The Alpenzeitung lists the 'Edenkino' up to 26 Nov 1935 and 'Cinema Luce (ex Edenkino)' from 27 Nov 1935 (Europeana full-text search, notes 15, §6, [V]); the League of Nations sanctions against Italy, approved on 3 Nov 1935, were to enter into force on 18 Nov (it.wikipedia, 'Oro alla Patria', [W])

A user comment on Cinema Treasures says the cinema 'temporarily changed its name to the Luce Cinema, due to Mussolini's political stance, which opposed that of British Prime Minister Antony Eden'; Eden was then the British minister for League of Nations affairs and became Foreign Secretary on 22 Dec 1935, prime minister only in 1955 (notes 15, §6, [S]; en.wikipedia, 'Anthony Eden', [W])

'Schülervorstellung im Centralkino': pupils of the Kgl. Handelsschule and the Handelsfortbildungskurs, with their teachers, attended 'einer Vorführung des prächtigen Dokumentarfilms „Von Adua nach Aksum“' (image, [V])
Same page: 'Zur Schaffung des neuen Stadt-Zentrums am Sieges-Denkmal', with a drawing, and 'Es ist eure Pflicht, Benzin zu sparen!' (image, [V])

entries.title: Il principe di Piemonte visita i nuovi lavori urbanistici e architettonici in corso a Bolzano (Giornale Luce B0967)
text: The Prince of Piedmont inspects Bolzano's building sites, 7 October 1936. A banner reads “Istituto case popolari di Bolzano. IV e V lotto”; an official shows him the plans of the new technical school; then “strada sventrata con lavori in corso” and “operai intenti alla demolizione di un edificio”.
The new city is filmed as plans, scaffolding and demolition. The old one appears as “case di Bolzano sullo sfondo di montagne”.

entries.title: Il ministro Benni e il conte Volpi inaugurano il nuovo centro industriale di Bolzano (Giornale Luce B1014)
text: The opening of the industrial zone, 23 December 1936, in one minute eleven. Minister Benni and Count Volpi visit Montecatini's aluminium exhibition and walk into a works marked “Lancia e C.”

The film goes straight on to “il nuovo quartiere per gli operai delle industrie” and a new building hung with banners praising Fascism and Mussolini. Factory and workers' housing are shown as one project.

entries.title: Radio italiana anno XVI [EIAR] (Istituto Luce documentary D032902)
text: A Luce film made with the state radio in 1937–38 on its stations, staff and broadcasts. After Turin, Milan, Trieste, Genoa, Florence and Bologna the catalogue lists “la stazione di Bolzano”, probably the building itself; that sequence has not been seen. Announcers “parlano in inglese e in tedesco”.
The frame held shows a microphone engraved with the dates of six broadcasts by the Duce, the king and the queen, 1935 to 1936.
facts: Code IL3000083387, film code D032902, 1937–38, 15'40", sound; 'Il film, realizzato in collaborazione con l'EIAR, mostra gli impianti, l'organizzazione, i protagonisti, l'attività della radio italiana' (record, [V])

After Turin, Milan, Trieste, Genoa, Florence and Bologna the record lists 'la stazione di Bolzano', before the short-wave station of Rome at Prato Smeraldo; the earlier notes took this for a map animation, but the record's surrounding lines are 'vedute degli impianti' of each station, so the film probably shows the Bolzano station itself (record, [V]; notes 02, §3; inference, [INF])
The film also shows 'annunciatori radiofonici al lavoro parlano in inglese e in tedesco' and the Radiocorriere coming off the presses (record, [V])

The frame shows six dates engraved on the microphone; 18 Dec 1935 is the 'Giornata della Fede', when Queen Elena was the first to give her wedding ring (it.wikipedia, 'Oro alla Patria', [W]); Luce filmed the Bolzano ceremony as 'La cerimonia dell'offerta delle Fedi Nuziali' (B0803, 24/12/1935) (notes 02, §1, [V])

Seen in the image: a cylindrical microphone engraved 'IL DUCE: 2 OTT. 1935-XIII / S.M. IL RE: 1 NOV. 1935-XIV / S.M. LA REGINA: 18 DIC. 1935-XIV / IL DUCE: 5 MAGGIO 1936-XIV / IL DUCE: 9 MAGGIO 1936-XIV / IL DUCE: 30 AGOSTO 1936-XIV'; timecode 'TCR 00:12:12:18'

entries.title: Il viaggio del Führer in Italia: "Dal Brennero a Roma" (Istituto Luce documentary D031201)
text: The first part of Luce's long film of Hitler's visit in May 1938, “Dal Brennero a Roma”. The train stops at the border station, “la svastica sul muso della locomotiva”. Then Bolzano: “una grande folla accoglie acclamante il passaggio del treno con l'illustre ospite; bandiere, fasci littori inneggiano al Fuhrer”.
Further down the line the catalogue notes a wall with “la scritta Heil Hitler” and the Nazi flag at the windows.
facts: Code IL3000084593, film code D031201, 1938, 1:49:17, sound, Italian; the first part 'Dal Brennero a Roma' runs 8'25" (record, [V])

Sequences: 'il treno si ferma alla stazione di confine del Brennero', 'la svastica sul muso della locomotiva', then 'la stazione di Bolzano – una grande folla accoglie acclamante il passaggio del treno con l'illustre ospite; bandiere, fasci littori inneggiano al Fuhrer' (record, [V])
Later on the route: 'sul muro di cinta la scritta Heil Hitler e alle finestre la bandiera nazista' (record, [V])
Luce's photographer Spartaco Appetiti photographed the same arrival at the Brenner and, from the train, the Cardano power station (row 15.16)

entries.title: Spartaco Appetiti (Istituto Luce), Hitler's arrival at the Brenner and the Cardano power station seen from the train, two photographs
text: Two of the fifteen photographs Luce's Spartaco Appetiti took of Hitler's arrival on 3 May 1938. On the Brenner platform Hitler stands with the Duke of Pistoia and Starace while a photographer in German uniform and one in fascist uniform take the scene.
The second was shot from the moving train: the hydroelectric station of Cardano, flags on its front. Of Bolzano he framed the power station.
facts: Story 'IL VIAGGIO DEL FUHRER IN ITALIA – I GIORNATA – ARRIVO – Al Brennero, lungo il percorso …', 15 photos found, 03.05.1938, author 'Appetiti, Spartaco' (records, [V])

A00082167: 'Hitler sulla banchina della stazione del Brennero con il Duca di Pistoia, Starace e varie autorità; un fotografo in divisa tedesca ed uno in divisa fascista riprendono la scena; ripresa dall'alto' (record, [V])
A00082180: 'La centrale idroelettrica di Cardano (comune di Bolzano) inquadrata dal treno in corsa' (record, [V])
From the train the photographer framed the city's power station, not its old town or its monument (record, [V]; reading, [INF])
Seen in the image (A00082167): Hitler in cap and uniform coat among officers in plumed helmets and a man in a black fascist uniform; at upper right two men hold cameras; watermark 'ISTITUTO LUCE'

Seen in the image (A00082180): a long building with flags on its façade and penstock pipes running down the hill behind it, a car on the road, a fence and rails in the foreground, the edge of a train window at left

entries.title: La celebrazione degli Altoatesini caduti (Giornale Luce B1312)
text: Starace in Bolzano on Sunday 22 May 1938, in a newsreel dated 1 June. At the monument the roll is called of “Altoatesini caduti nella guerra spagnola e in quella di Africa”: South Tyroleans dead in Spain and Africa, claimed by name for the nation. The film cuts to the border post on the Brenner, then to 500 cars parading through the city for a rally of the automobile club.
In the frame held, a car carries two horn loudspeakers on its roof.
facts: Giornale Luce B / B1312, code IL5000029437, clip B131204, 01/06/1938, 1'16", sound; direzione artistica Arnaldo Ricotti (record, [V])

Sequences: 'Starace accolto da una grande folla a Bolzano', 'il monumento ai caduti con i fasci littori', 'l'appello degli Altoatesini caduti nella guerra spagnola e in quella di Africa', 'la colonnina del confine del Brennero', '500 automobili sfilano per le strade di Bolzano', 'il raduno è stato indetto dal RACI' (record, [V])

The event filmed is the roll call of Sunday 22 May 1938 (Dolomiten, 23 May 1938, p. 1, row 17.15: Starace, 32 names, 500 cars of the automobile club); 1 June 1938 is the reel's catalogue date. An earlier version of this row gave 1 June as the day and took 'the 1938 column' for the Brenner boundary post of this reel; the column of 1938 is the Colonna Romana unveiled behind the monument on 5 June (row 17.16; film B1319) (notes 17, §7, [V] and [INF]; corrected 14 November 2026)

The dead called by name are South Tyroleans fallen in Spain and Africa (East Africa and Libya, by the names printed in Dolomiten on 23 May 1938): the regime's appeal claims them for the nation (record, [V]; reading, [INF])
Seen in the image: an arcaded street with parked cars; on the roof of the car at left two large horn loudspeakers; a tower with a clock closes the street; timecode '00:17:39:04'

entries.title: Istituto Luce, "Bolzano – Raduno di mutilati, vedove ed orfani altoatesini che esprimono riconoscenza al regime fascista", photograph
text: A Luce photograph filed on 4 September 1938: women in traditional dress holding bouquets, a crowd behind them, “probabilmente di fronte al Monumento della Vittoria”. It belongs to the rally at which war-disabled, widows and orphans of the old Austro-Hungarian army thanked the regime.
The catalogue files it under “Etnografia ed etnologia”.
facts: Code A00084968, the only photograph of its story, catalogue date 04.09.1938, place 'Bolzano', themes 'manifestazioni del regime fascista; Etnografia ed etnologia; La donna; balilla moschettieri; Politica sociale del fascismo'; photographer not named (record, [V])
Caption: 'Alcune donne in abiti tradizionali riprese con mazzi di fiori in mano, probabilmente di fronte al Monumento della Vittoria' (record, [V])
Luce filmed the same rally: Giornale Luce B1368 of 08/09/1938, row 15.19, in Piazza della Vittoria (record, [V])
The catalogue files the widows and orphans of the former Austro-Hungarian army under 'Etnografia ed etnologia' (record, [V])

Seen in the image: four women in dark bodices and aprons, two in light patterned aprons, hold large bouquets; a crowd behind, boys in black caps among them; a man in a dark suit at the right edge; watermark 'ISTITUTO LUCE'

entries.title: Manifestazione di 'riconoscenza' dei mutilati ed orfani di guerra dell'ex esercito austro-ungarico verso il regime fascista (Giornale Luce B1368)
text: The Luce newsreel of the same rally, 8 September 1938, two minutes fourteen. In the rain, under umbrellas, the war-disabled and orphans “dell'ex esercito austro-ungarico” crowd Piazza della Vittoria to thank the regime for measures in their favour; “un fascista ordina il saluto a Mussolini e la gente lo esegue”.
It is the only Luce film found in which South Tyroleans appear as political subjects, and they appear grateful. The Berlin conference that led to the Option came ten months later.
facts: Giornale Luce B / B1368, code IL5000028666, clip B136808, 08/09/1938, 2'14", sound; direzione artistica Arturo Gemmiti; full title adds 'per i provvedimenti governativi in loro favore, alla presenza del Duca di Pistoia e del politico Delcroix' (record, [V])

Sequences: 'la folla si accalca nella piazza della Vittoria intorno ad un arco di costruzione del regime fascista, monumento ai caduti', 'la folla nella piazza con gli ombrelli aperti per ripararsi dalla pioggia', Delcroix speaking, 'un fascista ordina il saluto a Mussolini e la gente lo esegue', a march past under the balcony of the 'palazzo del governo' (record, [V])
The only Luce film found in which South Tyroleans appear as political subjects, framed as grateful (notes 02, §1, [I])
It came out ten months before the Berlin conference of 23 June 1939 from which the Option came (notes 04, §4, [V]); the quotation marks around 'riconoscenza' are in the catalogue title (record, [V])
Seen in the image: a row of people, men in uniform and caps among them, stand before a monument hung with flags and banners; a microphone on a stand; flowers on the ground in front; LUCE logo

entries.title: Il ponte del Littorio (Giornale Luce B1540)
text: Minister Cobolli Gigli and Prefect Mastromattei open the Ponte Littorio over the Isarco, 5 July 1939: “il ponte unisce la zona industriale con il villaggio delle case popolari e la via Roma”. The minister then fires the charge that starts the tunnel through the Virgolo.
Which of today's bridges it is has not been established.

Sequences: 'il ministro Cobolli Gigli e il prefetto Mastromattei hanno inaugurato il ponte Littorio sul fiume Isarco', 'il ponte unisce la zona industriale con il villaggio delle case popolari e la via Roma', 'alcuni edifici governativi e le case popolari', 'il ministro ha dato il via alla costruzione della galleria che attraverserà il colle del Virgolo azionando la mina', 'la galleria sarà funzionale alla strada del Brennero' (record, [V])
Which bridge of today the 'ponte del Littorio' is was not established (notes 15, §1, Gaps)

entries.title: "Una superba realizzazione del Regime per il benessere dei lavoratori nella provincia del Brennero": the Rione Popolare Dux (Giornale Luce B1599)
text: The Semirurali on film, 11 October 1939: “il salubre e ridente Rione Popolare Dux che ultimato consterà di 228 casette con 808 appartamenti e 8 negozi”, opened by the party secretary. Two-storey houses with a plot each, a priest blessing the quarter, the vegetable gardens.
The title calls the province “provincia del Brennero”. The film came out ten days before the rules of the Option were issued and does not mention it.
facts: Giornale Luce B / B1599, code IL5000022261, clip B159907, 11/10/1939, 1'30", sound; direzione artistica Arturo Gemmiti (record, [V])

The title, in quotation marks in the record: 'Una superba realizzazione del Regime per il benessere dei lavoratori nella provincia del Brennero, inaugurata dal Ministro Segretario del Partito…il salubre e ridente Rione Popolare Dux che ultimato consterà di 228 casette con 808 appartamenti e 8 negozi' (record, [V])

The province is called 'provincia del Brennero' in the title, as in Luce photo captions ('Gagliardetto del Brennero', 1931) (record; row 15.03, [V])
Released on 11 Oct 1939, ten days before the Option's implementing 'Richtlinien' of 21 Oct 1939; the record does not mention the Option (record; notes 04, §4, [V])

entries.title: "L'incontro fra il Duce e il Fuehrer" at the Brenner, 18 March 1940 (Giornale Luce B1692)
text: Hitler and Mussolini meet at the Brenner on 18 March 1940; the newsreel is dated the 22nd. Snow on the station, Hitler's train arriving, the handshake, soldiers guarding the train as it snows, “Mussolini fa il saluto fascista, Ciano osserva il treno allontanarsi”.
British newsreels carried the same meeting, known here from a search result only.
facts: Giornale Luce B / B1692, code IL5000024850, clip B169207, 22/03/1940, 1'39", sound; direzione artistica Basilio Franchina; the YouTube title dates the meeting '18 marzo 1940' (record; manifest, [V])

British newsreels carried the same meeting ('Dictators Meet at Brenner Pass', Pathé Gazette 40/26, 28 March 1940, per a search result only) (notes 15, §3, [SS])

entries.title: Istituto Luce, "Brennero – L'incontro del Duce con il Fuerher alla presenza dei ministri degli esteri Conte Ciano e von Ribbentrop", two photographs
text: Two of seven Luce photographs of the second Brenner meeting, 4 October 1940. Hitler and Mussolini walk the platform past soldiers presenting arms; then, in a railway carriage with curtained windows, they sit at a table with a lace cloth, Ciano beside them.
No Luce film of this meeting was found. These photographs are its record.

entries.title: Ministero della Cultura Popolare, nulla osta no. 31160 for "Il ribelle della montagna (Der Feuerteufel)"
text: The censorship visa for Luis Trenker's “Der Feuerteufel”, passed in November 1940 as “Il ribelle della montagna”. The ministry's synopsis sets it in Carinthia: “uno spaccalegna della Carinzia” who led “una sommossa popolare nella Carinzia” under Napoleon's tyranny over Germany.
The first research pass, following Wikipedia, had placed the film in the Tyrolean rising of 1809. Unlike his films of 1935 and 1937, this one carries no ban for Bolzano and Trento.
facts: Censorship visa: 'Ministero della Cultura Popolare – Direzione generale per la cinematografia', 'N. di prot. 31160', 'Titolo: Il ribelle della montagna (Der Feuerteufel)', 'Produzione: Bavaria Filmkunst', 'Regia: Luis Trenker', metres declared and checked 2542 (file, [V])
Italia Taglia gives the dates 13 and 22 November 1940 and 'Approvata'; the sheet is a duplicate issued at Rome with a date stamp read as '4 DIC. 1940' (file; row 15.01, [V])

The Ministry's synopsis sets the film in Carinthia: 'uno spaccalegna della Carinzia, Valentino Sturmegger il quale, durante la tirannia napoleonica sulla Germania, capeggiava una sommossa popolare nella Carinzia' (file, [V])
This contradicts the earlier notes, which placed 'Der Feuerteufel' in the 1809 Tyrolean rising after English Wikipedia (notes 02, §2, [S]; this file, [V])
Unlike Trenker's 1935 and 1936–37 films, no ban for the provinces of Bolzano and Trento is recorded for this one (row 15.01, [V])

Seen in the image: a printed ministry form with a crest, the title line, a two-column 'Descrizione del soggetto', a round stamp at upper right, the conditions of the nulla osta in small type and a signature 'Pel Ministro'

entries.title: Istituto Luce, "Bolzano – Terza asta nazionale di pelli pregiate di produzione italiana", two photographs
text: Wartime Bolzano as a trade fair: two Luce photographs of 16 January 1942. A poster announces the national exhibition and sale of furs “di produzione nazionale”; in the hall of the Palazzo Mercantile, under chandeliers, rows of fur traders follow the auction.
Luce filed the story under “Autarchia”. It is the only Luce record of a fair in Bolzano before 1945 found so far.
facts: Story of 4 photos, 16.01.1942, place 'Bolzano', themes 'Autarchia; Fiere ed esposizioni; Zootecnia; Allevamento di animali da pelliccia; Sindacati fascisti'; photographer not named (records A00138634 to A00138637, [V])

A00138637: 'Salone del Palazzo Mercantile di Bolzano gremito di commercianti e industriali di pellicce per l'asta organizzata dalla Federazione nazionale dei consorzi provinciali tra i produttori dell'agricoltura' (record, [V])

The earlier notes found no Luce film of a Bolzano fair before 1945 and the 'Palazzo Mercantile' tag only on post-war items; this wartime trade exhibition is a Luce photo story (notes 02, §1, [V]; row 15.03)
Fur farming in the province recurs in Luce newsreels of 1932, 1939 and 1940 (Collalbo silver foxes, black mink) (notes 02, newsreel table, [V])

Seen in the image (A00138634): a poster reading 'Federazione nazionale dei consorzi provinciali tra i produttori dell'agricoltura – Settore della zootecnia – Esposizione-vendita nazionale di pelli di animali da pelliccia di produzione nazionale – Bolzano 16 gennaio 1942-XX', under a crowned crest
Seen in the image (A00138637): rows of seated men holding papers in a hall with chandeliers, wall lamps and paintings; a man standing at right reads from a sheet
